head: b4dff46aeba81822ac2bb2d75189060d7bcf61bb
answers: Review round 6's request for changes, which the architect turned into review round 7 of dispatch://INFRA-484/artifact/review-rounds-md v10: a round, once opened, ends only by replacing its pod, or because that pod is gone.

proof.criterion: Item 1. A round, once opened, ends only by replacing its pod. The drift clearing under an open round no longer ends it: the pod is replaced all the same, the answered worker is told nothing, and the no-replacement ending (the drift-cleared branch, podUpdateOverTask, tellRoundIsOver, Machine.roundOver and its run in afterTurn, PodUpdateEnded.Replaced, and the release of answered workers) is deleted.
proof.surface: The whole Legion daemon as `legion start` runs it: run() over a real PostgreSQL carrying this branch's migrations, its real HTTP API on a real listener, its real worker-stream listener, the real supervision, the real claim machines and the real orphan sweep at 250 ms, with internal/runtime/fake as the cluster and an in-process nats-server for the outbox the sweep writes through. Both workers of the issue are real shim connections over the worker stream; the implementer answers over the real POST /legion/v1/claims/ready-for-update route and the tester, on plugin contract 44, by ending the turn its task started.
proof.observed: PROOF step 1: both roles run in one pod; the implementer speaks plugin contract 45 and the tester 44, which is below the 45 that added ready_for_update. PROOF step 1: implementer was asked: "The daemon must replace the pod that runs this issue's roles. The reasons are: image ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker@sha25…", the same for the tester, and the below-contract tester's task names the fallback: "If your `legion` tool has no \"ready_for_update\" operation, do step 1 and step 3 only." PROOF step 1: ReplacePod has been called 0 times while the round waits for its two answers. PROOF step 2: the drift of pod 00000001-… went away — the operator rolled the release back — and sweeps have read it drifted from nothing, with the round still open. PROOF step 2: the pod was replaced all the same: ReplacePod ran once, over the round's own pod, with no drift left to replace it for (decision 1). PROOF step 2: the round ended on both claims and neither worker was sent anything — no "carry on", no "the round is over" — in 2s of sweeps. PROOF step 2: the daemon wrote nothing on the issue and told the controller nothing: its own outbox holds no dispatch_message and no controller_notice row of the issue, and Dispatch received no message. --- PASS: TestINFRA484Round7UpdateRoundProof (17.32s).
proof.negativeControl: The regression lock TestPodUpdateReplacesThePodWhenTheDriftClearsUnderAnOpenRound was run with the fix reverted, in a throwaway copy of the tree under $TMPDIR and never in the branch: with the drift-cleared early end restored in reconcileIssuePodUpdate it fails, `podupdate_test.go:718: ReplacePod called 0 times once the drift had gone away, want the one replacement the round was opened for`, and it passes at the head.

proof.criterion: Item 2. A gone pod ends the round at the first sweep that reads runtime.ErrPodGone: the lost-work report is decided from the answers recorded at that moment and the round is cleared on every claim in the same pass, so nothing in the pod that replaced it can change the report afterwards. A pod whose Sandbox is suspended or terminating by this round's own ReplacePod counts as replaced; any other suspended Sandbox counts as gone.
proof.surface: The same whole-daemon surface, on a second issue of the same run: a round open over its pod with one worker answered and one not, the runtime then scripted to answer runtime.ErrPodGone for that pod, and the unanswered worker answering over the real ready-for-update route after the gone read. The suspended-Sandbox half is driven against the fake dynamic client in internal/runtime/sandbox, which is where PodDrift reads a real Sandbox object.
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=postgres://legion_test@127.0.0.1:5433/legion_infra484_r7?sslmode=disable go test ./internal/daemon/ -run TestINFRA484Round7UpdateRoundProof -count=1 -v; and cd packages/daemon && go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox/ -run TestPodDriftReadsASuspendedSandboxAsItsOwnReplacementOrAsAGonePod -count=1 -v
proof.observed: PROOF step 3: at the sweep that read runtime.ErrPodGone the daemon wrote on the issue exactly once, naming the worker that had not answered: "The pod that ran this issue's roles is gone. The daemon opened an update round over that pod (pod:00000002-2b4…". PROOF step 3: the daemon's own outbox table held exactly one dispatch_message row of that issue at the moment that message was posted. PROOF step 3: the round was cleared on every claim in that same pass, and nothing was replaced — the round ended on the gone pod alone (decision 2). PROOF step 3: the worker that had not answered answered after the gone read; the daemon refused it (409: ready_for_update refused: the answer names an update round this claim is not in) and the report did not change — still one message on the issue. The sandbox half: ok github.com/sjawhar/legion/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox, with the suspended Sandbox naming this round's own displaced pod read as a pod that has not drifted and every other suspended Sandbox read as runtime.ErrPodGone.
proof.negativeControl: PROOF negative control, in the same run: the same gone pod with the second worker's answer given before the gone read instead of after it gives the other report — every worker answered, nothing was lost, the issue was written on 0 times where step 3's issue was written on once, and nothing was replaced, so the gone read is what ended both rounds. And the two regression locks were run with the fix reverted in a throwaway copy of the tree under $TMPDIR: with groupDrift's ErrPodGone branch removed, TestPodUpdateEndsTheRoundAtTheFirstReadOfAGonePod fails `podupdate_test.go:846: the issue was written on 0 times at the sweep that read the pod gone, want once for the pod that went` and TestPodUpdateEndsAGonePodsRoundWithNoMessageWhenEveryWorkerAnswered fails `podupdate_test.go:921: timed out waiting for implementer: its round to end at the sweep that read its pod gone`; with the displaced-annotation test removed from drift.go, TestPodDriftReadsASuspendedSandboxAsItsOwnReplacementOrAsAGonePod fails `drift_test.go:421: PodDrift of a suspended sandbox naming no replaced pod = [], <nil>; want runtime.ErrPodGone`.

proof.criterion: Item 3. A task an open round holds is never confirmed by a turn, after a daemon restart too: it stays pending and unconfirmed until the pod is replaced, and is delivered then.
proof.surface: The same whole-daemon surface, on a third issue: a round open with every worker answered and a task queued for each, the daemon then stopped and started again on the same store, one turn of another cause driven over the real shim connection, and the pod replaced at the end.
proof.observed: PROOF step 4: the round holds each answered worker's next task: both are pending and unsent after 2s of sweeps. PROOF step 4: the daemon was stopped and started again on the same store. PROOF step 4: both held tasks came back pending and unconfirmed after the restart. PROOF step 4: one turn of another cause ran and ended on the implementer; its held task "review the pull request" is still pending and unconfirmed — not that turn's task, and not retired (decision 3). PROOF step 4: the tester's answer still stands, so the round still holds its task: pending, unsent and unconfirmed after 2s more of sweeps. PROOF step 4: every worker answered and the pod was replaced once. PROOF step 4: the task the round held for the tester is delivered once the pod is replaced: it read "run the tests again".
proof.negativeControl: The regression lock TestPodUpdateARestartLeavesTheHeldTaskToNoTurnButItsOwn was run with the fix reverted, in a throwaway copy of the tree under $TMPDIR: with `&& !c.openRoundHoldsTask()` dropped from NewMachine's askFirst it fails, `podupdate_test.go:406: the notice's turn was taken as the held task's: &{ID:LQ7JMRH2UBRDRFDNEJJ7FWAIJC Task:review the pull request … ConfirmedAt:2026-09-22 12:00:00 +0000 UTC …}; no daemon ever sent that task`, and it passes at the head.

proof.criterion: Item 4, first minor. The late notice is not sent when its waiting list is empty: a round whose only waiting claim was counted waiting because its machine was deciding reads, unmasked, as every claim answered, and such a round is not stalled.
proof.surface: The daemon's own sweep over a real PostgreSQL with a real claim machine mid-decision, reading the refusals out of the sweep's own log and the daemon's outbox table.
proof.observed: Both cases pass: the claim mid-decision draws no notice and no refusal, and a claim that really has not answered still draws the notice naming it. --- PASS: TestPodUpdateTellsNobodyOfARoundWaitingOnlyOnAClaimMidDecision.
proof.negativeControl: Run with the fix reverted in a throwaway copy of the tree under $TMPDIR: with the empty-waiting guard removed from the unmasked read, it fails `podupdate_test.go:2046: the sweep logged 1 refused notices, want none: [… error: enqueue a controller_notice row of LEGION-484: an update-stalled notice requires its round and the claims it waits on …]`.

proof.criterion: Item 4, second minor. The Claude Code exemption from the stale-plugin relaunch is the Kubernetes runtime's alone: under tmux a relaunch rereads LEGION_CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DIR, so a tmux Claude Code pane relaunches once its turn ends, as an Oh My Pi worker does.
proof.surface: The daemon's stale-plugin lane over a real PostgreSQL, run once with the deployment's runtime set to kubernetes and once to tmux, with the role on the claude backend in both.
proof.observed: Both subtests pass: under kubernetes the Claude Code worker is left running and served on its own contract, and under tmux it is relaunched once its turn ends.
proof.negativeControl: Run with the fix reverted in a throwaway copy of the tree under $TMPDIR: with the runtime test dropped from noPluginInstall, the tmux subtest fails `podupdate_test.go:1603: timed out waiting for implementer: the worker a relaunch can carry past the contract to be relaunched`.

proof.criterion: Item 5. The guide, the role prompts, the worker skill, the two plugins' prose and the changelog fragments say the round ends only by replacement.
proof.surface: The repository's own structural tests over the embedded role prompts and the plugins' staged skill partitions, and the changelog fold's own gate over the fragments.

proof.negativeControl: Before the fragment fix, the same fold-orphans command is the `lint` job's red of CI run 41317023541: `release-push.sh fold-orphans: packages/daemon/.changes/unreleased/INFRA-484-stale-plugin-waits-for-the-turn.yaml packages/daemon/.changes/unreleased/INFRA-484-the-update-round.yaml at HEAD: each is under the .changes/ of a package the fold was not given`.

docs/kubernetes.md, packages/daemon/internal/prompts/go/architect-common.md and worker-common.md, skills/legion-worker/SKILL.md, packages/claude-envoy/AGENTS.md, packages/pi-shared/src/phase-reminder.ts and phase-stall.ts with their tests, and the changelog fragments: the round ends only by replacing its pod.

trickyParts: Items 1 to 5 were already committed on the branch when this session began (c865e10861eb, 706030f0cac1, 7ff3980816cb, 5eb1a70a26ac, adfba09b3c54): the previous session was cleared by the model provider at 14:57Z after writing them. This session verified each against the round-7 decision rather than redoing it, added the red-run evidence for every one, answered and resolved the six open threads, merged main twice, and ran the whole-daemon proof.

Every red run was made in a throwaway copy of the tree under $TMPDIR (/legion/scratch/tmp/infra484-redrun), never in the branch, because reverting a deletion means restoring code the branch no longer holds. The workspace was never left in a reverted state.

Item 1's revert for the red run restores only the drift-cleared early end in reconcileIssuePodUpdate, which is the one branch the test pins; the rest of the deleted ending has no test of its own left, since those tests were deleted with the path they pinned, as the architect's decision asked.
deviations: Migration 0068 could not be kept, against the architect's first instruction, and the architect accepted the reason at 19:14Z. main closed the daemon's numbered migration series at 0067 (packages/envoy/migrationid/migrationid.go:52 on 0642a37a), and #2633 moved only Dispatch's closing, from 0157 to 0161. Every store the merged tree migrates refuses 0068: CI run 41317023541 failed 1341 tests, each reading `migration 0068_claim_pod_update.up.sql takes version 68: the numbered migrations ended at 67`. The file is renamed for the UTC moment it was written, 20261029195520_claim_pod_update.up.sql (commit 63beb7bd80ea, 2026-10-29T19:55:20Z). Contract 45 is unchanged, as instructed.

The two daemon changelog fragments were removed rather than rewritten: packages/daemon has no .changie.yaml and is in no CHANGELOG_PACKAGES spec, so the fold folds nothing there and release-push.sh fold-orphans refuses a fragment left under it, which was the same CI run's lint red. What they said is in docs/kubernetes.md, which this branch already carries.

Two forward merges this round, both recorded on the pull request as the skill requires. The first (main 8d555cc2) was taken because the branch's only red test job was main's new migration rule meeting this branch's file, which is the 'needs something only the base has' trigger; it moved the changed-file set from 137 to 135 and the fingerprint from 155b8aaca9419bc84a1a9b5c78d78a3ea90e3c94e974ed8547f9a5b17af6d3df to 8f9ad4bd677a62e21202d75b1ace0cb1c1536c4530a32ae1cb08942dd94d24bd. Every file is accounted for: four renames (the migration and three fragments) and two removals (the daemon fragments), nothing else left or joined. The second (main 0642a37a) was taken at the architect's instruction and changed neither the fingerprint nor the file set, so it is a confirmation rather than a new round. The proof was run again at the merge head.
openQuestions: sjawhar/legion#2539 (INFRA-714) adds the changelog fold for packages/daemon. The architect's instruction of 19:14Z: whichever of #2538 and #2539 merges second restores this change's two daemon entries as packages/daemon/.changes/unreleased/pr2538-<slug>.yaml, taken from this branch's history, where commits 5eb1a70a26ac and c865e10861eb carry their text. discoveredComplexity: The pod's shared PostgreSQL (LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN) refuses `drop database … with (force)` in a test's t.Cleanup while a sibling role of the pod holds a connection, because legion_test is not a superuser and cannot signal a backend of another login: `outbox_integration_test.go:229: drop legion_outbox_test_…: ERROR: permission denied to terminate process (SQLSTATE 42501)`. Every such failure is in teardown and never an assertion; which tests show it varies between runs. CI runs its own PostgreSQL and does not have it.

Three suites cannot run in this pod at all, for the environment and not for the change: internal/runtime/tmux's TestNewRefusesLaunchersItCannotRun (tmux is not installed), any internal/daemon or internal/workflow test that starts a NATS testcontainer (docker is not available; the proof driver works around it with an in-process nats-server), and pi-legion's judge-omp rig in scripts/skill-scenarios (each judge runs in a container).
